title: Movie Night
story: You're inviting your best friend Jordan to watch a movie on Saturday. You want to write a program that builds the perfect invitation message by gluing together pieces of text � the friend's name, the movie title, and the time. No more typing the same message over and over!
why: Building strings from smaller pieces lets you create personalized messages without retyping everything. It's how apps send custom emails, notifications, and greetings.
analogy: String concatenation is like building a train � each car holds a piece of text, and you hook them together one at a time to make a longer train.
try_it: Change the movie title to your favorite movie and run the program again. Now try inviting a different friend by changing the `friend` variable. Can you add a time, like "at 7pm", to the invitation?
tips: `string.str_concat(a, b)` takes exactly two strings and returns them glued together.
Don't forget spaces inside your text pieces: `"Hey "` has a space at the end so words don't run together.
You can chain concatenations: use the result of one `string.str_concat` as input to the next one.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to include the space after a word: `string.str_concat("Hey", friend)` produces `"HeyJordan"` without a space.
Trying to concatenate a number with a string � `string.str_concat("Age: ", 14)` won't work because 14 is an Int, not a Str.
Passing only one argument to `string.str_concat` � it always needs exactly two strings.
